program: Business English — Corporate Communication in a Global Airline
hub_subtitle: Reunião regional, e-mail corporativo, treinamento global e convenção internacional

lesson.menu_title: You Should, You Could, You Must — The Rule and the Exception
lesson.menu_desc: Modals for obligation, advice and deduction, in the call where the client wants an exception -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- You Should, You Could, You Must
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 7 -- You Should, You Could, You Must
lesson.grammar_point: modal verbs for obligation, advice and deduction

listenings.text: Rosa, this is Gustavo from the travel desk. I have a problem and I do not think you can solve it, but I have to ask anyway. We booked twelve people on the Tuesday flight and the meeting moved to Thursday. The fare rules say we must pay a change fee on every ticket, which is more than the tickets cost us in the first place. I know I should have called you before we booked, and I did not. So my question is simple. Is there anything you can do, and if there is not, could you at least tell me what I should do differently next time? I would rather learn the rule than argue with it.

Two minutes on corporate policy, because this comes up on every call. There are three levels and people mix them up constantly. Level one, the rule. If the contract says the change fee applies, it applies, and none of us can remove it by being sympathetic. Level two, the guidelines. These are recommendations, not obligations, and you can depart from them if you can explain why. Level three, the exception. An exception must be requested, it must have a reason attached, and it must be approved by somebody above you. What you must never do is promise the exception before it is approved. If you do that, you have not helped the client. You have simply moved the bad news to somebody else's phone call.

items.situation: A client asks you to remove a change fee that the contract clearly applies.
tips: Must for the rule, could for the alternative
The fee applies, but we could look at the fare instead

items.situation: A colleague asks whether she needs to copy the regional office on every email.
tips: Do not have to is not the same as must not
You do not have to copy them, but you should on anything over the limit

items.situation: The client asks what he should do differently next time.
tips: Should plus base verb, one concrete action
You should call me before you book twelve seats

items.situation: You do not know why the system rejected the booking.
tips: Might and could for a guess you are not sure about
It might be the fare class -- let me check and call you back

items.situation: Somebody asks you to promise an exception you cannot approve.
tips: Say what you can do, not what you cannot
I cannot approve it, but I can escalate it today

items.situation: The numbers on the invoice are clearly wrong.
tips: That must be the old fare -- the contract changed in March

extra_audio.text: Gustavo explains that the meeting moved and that twelve tickets now have to be changed. Rosa says that the change fee applies under the contract and that she cannot remove it. Gustavo asks whether there is anything at all that can be done. Rosa offers to escalate a waiver request and explains what has to go with it. Gustavo asks what he should do differently next time, and Rosa gives him one concrete rule about calling before booking a group.
